ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure, there is an input R(s) entering a summing point, and the R(s) terminal is marked with a positive sign; the feedback terminal returning to this summing point from below is marked with a negative sign. The output of the left summing point splits into upper and lower paths, respectively entering two identical transfer function blocks 1/(s+1). The output of the upper block goes right as Y(s), and also connects downward to the positive input of the right summing point. The output of the lower block connects to the negative input of the right summing point. The output of the right summing point feeds back along the bottom to the negative input of the left summing point. Reasoning: Let the output of the left summing point be E(s). Since the upper and lower two blocks are identical, the upper output Y(s)=E(s)/(s+1), and the lower output is also E(s)/(s+1). The feedback signal produced by the right summing point is the upper output minus the lower output, namely E(s)/(s+1)-E(s)/(s+1)=0. Therefore the output of the left summing point E(s)=R(s)-0=R(s). Substitute into Y(s)=E(s)/(s+1), obtaining Y(s)/R(s)=1/(s+1).

method.method_draft: Let E(s) be the output of the left summing junction. From the two identical blocks, the upper output is Y(s)=E(s)/(s+1), and the lower output is also E(s)/(s+1). The feedback signal produced by the right summing junction is the signed difference of these two branch outputs, so it is E(s)/(s+1)-E(s)/(s+1)=0. Therefore the left summing junction output is E(s)=R(s)-0=R(s). Substitute into Y(s)=E(s)/(s+1) to obtain Y(s)/R(s)=1/(s+1).

method.method_draft: View the right-side feedback-producing network as a signed parallel combination from the left-summer output to the feedback line. Its equivalent transfer is 1/(s+1) - 1/(s+1) = 0 because the two blocks are identical and enter the right summing junction with opposite signs. Thus the outer feedback loop is effectively absent. The remaining forward path from R(s) to Y(s) is just the upper block 1/(s+1), so Y(s)/R(s)=1/(s+1).
